messages:
From: Anna Hsu <anna.hsu@starliteanalytics.com>

Cc: finance@starliteanalytics.com, Marco Rossi <m.rossi@starliteanalytics.eu>

Subject: VAT treatment for Redwood invoices / request for self-billing

Hi Logan,

Quick one from finance as we're getting the PO in place (PO-4221). We have multiple entities across the EU/UK and need to confirm the correct VAT handling before we approve payment. Specifically:  
- Which Redwood legal entity should receive the invoices for services delivered to our UK subsidiary vs. our Ireland entity?
- Will you apply reverse-charge on invoices to our Ireland (B2B) entity if we provide a valid VAT ID?
- We can also do self-billing if Redwood is able to accept — do you have a template and sign-off person?

I've attached a CSV of our VAT IDs and the PO. Can you confirm the approach and any documents you need for validation?

Thanks,
Anna Hsu
Head of Finance (Starlite Analytics)
anna.hsu@starliteanalytics.com
+44 20 5555 1212

Attachments: starlite-vat-ids.csv (text/csv), PO-4221.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Anna Hsu <anna.hsu@starliteanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: VAT treatment for Redwood invoices / request for self-billing

Hi Anna — thanks for the CSV and the PO. Looping in Karthik (billing ops) and Priya (payments) to map this out. Quick summary up-front:

- For B2B supplies to an EU customer with a valid VAT ID (Ireland), Redwood will issue an invoice net of VAT and apply the reverse-charge mechanism; we need the VAT ID validated and a customer contact on the invoice.
- For the UK entity, depending on whether the purchase is routed through our UK-registered entity or through our EU entity, VAT treatment differs — we typically bill the UK entity from Redwood Ltd (UK) and apply UK VAT rules; if the UK entity is B2B and provides a UK VAT registration we can consider reverse-charge where applicable, but we'll confirm with billing.
- We can support self-billing. I've attached our self-billing template and the internal sign-off path. Priya will confirm the acceptance checklist and next steps for sign-off and archiving.

Action items for you: please confirm the invoice remit-to entity (which of your entities should receive Redwood invoices) and confirm the primary VAT contact for each entity. Once we validate the VAT numbers we'll update the invoice templates and proceed with PO-4221.

Karthik/Priya: please advise if we should route the Ireland invoices to Redwood EMEA (IE) or Redwood Inc (US) for this contract and whether to auto-apply reverse-charge once validation completes.

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0199

Attachments: redwood-self-billing-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Hsu <anna.hsu@starliteanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:25:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal: proposed billing-entity mapping for Starlite (PO-4221)

Logan / Priya — I reviewed the VAT IDs in the CSV and here is my recommended mapping based on entity country and current tax registrations: 

1) Starlite Analytics Ireland Ltd (IE VAT: IE1234567) — bill from Redwood EMEA (Ireland) and apply reverse-charge (net invoice). Require VAT validation screenshot and company registration number.
2) Starlite Analytics UK Ltd (GB VAT: GB7654321) — bill from Redwood Ltd (UK). If the UK entity flags B2B with valid VAT, we can zero-rate where local rules allow, but we'll likely need to charge VAT at point of supply unless they provide evidence for reverse-charge.
3) For any centralized procurement entity (Starlite Group Ltd) — route to Redwood Inc (US) only if they confirm non-EU taxable status. This is uncommon and requires tax sign-off.

Please note: our system will require an approved VAT-exempt flag per customer entity before issuing net invoices; otherwise VAT will be included by default. If Starlite wants us to backdate any credits related to previous invoices, they must complete the VAT validation and sign the self-billing agreement first.

I recommend: 1) accept the self-billing template and sign it, 2) we validate the VAT IDs via VIES and collect proof, 3) switch future invoices to reverse-charge where applicable and credit any invoices issued in error after sign-off.

-Karthik
Billing Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

- UK entity (GB7654321) will be billed via Redwood Ltd; I'll follow up with our UK tax team to see if they can provide additional evidence for reverse-charge, but please proceed with standard UK billing for now.

Subject: Re: VAT treatment for Redwood invoices / request for self-billing — confirmation and next steps

Anna — thanks for the updated CSV and the signed PO. Finalizing next steps below: 

1) Redwood will run VAT ID validations via VIES and local registry checks by EOD Mon (2026-09-14). Please confirm any secondary VAT IDs in the updated CSV if present.
2) Once validated we will:  
   - Flag the Ireland entity as VAT-exempt (reverse-charge) and issue future invoices net of VAT.
   - Keep the UK entity on standard billing until we receive additional evidence; we will not reissue historic UK invoices automatically.
3) Self-billing: we can accept Starlite's consent via the attached template. Please sign the redwood-self-billing-template.xlsx and return; the internal finance approver is Priya N. (CC'd).
4) Payment collection: once invoices are issued we will use the remit-to in the signed PO-4221; payment terms remain Net30 unless you request otherwise.

I'll circulate the validation results and the finalized invoice routing by Tue 09/15. If you need a credit for any invoices incorrectly charged VAT post-validation, send the invoice numbers and we'll evaluate credits after validation completes.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Manager, Payments & Treasury
Redwood Inference
